# ASU thesis chapter structure and research-completion behavior
**Adopted 2026-10-09 — guidance, not institutional chapter-count requirement**

## Institutional vs recommended
ASU Graduate College formatting and required components are controlled by the current official Format Manual, Format Wizard and academic-unit/committee requirements; **ASU does not prescribe a universal fixed chapter count for all master's theses**. Verify current policies and chair decisions at submission time. The **seven-chapter organization below is a recommended internal architecture**, not ASU policy, not an independently frozen scientific objective and not evidence of manuscript completion.

Official starting point: https://graduate.asu.edu/current-students/completing-your-degree/formatting-your-thesis-or-dissertation/asu-graduate-college
Internal institutional controls: `thesis/00_governance/ASU_REQUIREMENTS_MATRIX.md`.
Current thesis authorities: `project/CURRENT_THESIS_AUTHORITY_INDEX_V1.md` and frozen GO/SO1–SO3.

## Proposed seven chapters (subject to thesis chair approval)
| Chapter | Required scientific function | Research gate |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Introduction | Engineering problem, sourced motivation, defensible gap, frozen objectives, questions and scope | literature-grounded problem; never manufacture novelty |
| 2 Literature Review and Theoretical Foundations | critical paper comparison, physical and mathematical prior arts, contradictions, source verification | primary-source and closest-prior-art audit |
| 3 System Architecture and Mathematical Framework | P/T_e composition, physical interfaces, governing laws, states/units, constraints, admissible model | case-specific law and state/parameter admission |
| 4 Research Methodology | case, data, estimation, comparison models, algorithm, verification, validation and uncertainty protocol | predeclared methods and reproducible implementation |
| 5 Results | **actual** verified numerical/empirical outputs, timing, uncertainty and service effects; negative outcomes | no filler/mock values as evidence |
| 6 Discussion | interpretations, rival explanations, comparison to prior art, limitations, scope of transfer | must follow genuine results |
| 7 Conclusions and Recommendations | answer RQs only to evidence extent, contributions and limitations | no unsupported claim of achievement |

Front matter, references and appendices remain required according to applicable ASU and chair specifications irrespective of chapter count. A six-chapter alternative can merge an appropriate pair of chapters if approved; this is an editorial decision, not a different physics objective.

## Dossiya Expert operating procedure
1. **Expert mode, not automatic tutoring:** Apply these rules when user requests thesis planning, chapter design, drafting or research execution. Do not start lessons/quizzes unless explicitly asked.
2. **Research before prose:** The two evaluated mock manuscripts are *working drafts*, not validated research outputs. Preserve scientific argument clarity from A and traceability/qualification strength from B, without freezing a disputed numerical grade or multiplying mock drafts.
3. **One master:** Maintain one active manuscript aligned to current canonical October 2026 thermal scope; preserve historical drafts separately. In-text scholarly citations immediately adjacent to external claims, with verified exact author/date and references. Repository-sourced provisional results remain labeled.
4. **Gate order:** (a) closest prior art and justified gap; (b) case/equipment and directional mechanisms; (c) minimum defensible physical model, parameters, units; (d) data/calibration vs independent validation; (e) tested computational solver; (f) matched experiments, uncertainty and results; (g) interpretation, final manuscript and ASU review. Independent nonblocked tasks may proceed in parallel, but their gate cannot be declared passed early.
5. **M0/M1/M2 authority:** independent / static-algebraic / evidence-qualified dynamic causal. Shared extreme heat != directional causation. EVSE AC draw affecting transformer losses does not imply power-to-transport derating without an actual operating law.
6. **Chapter dependency:** Chapters 1–4 may be drafted as evidence matures; Chapters 5–7 must present *actual* executed findings and bounded answers. Write final abstract after results. Verification != empirical validation; merge != scientific approval.
7. **Submission:** Recheck current ASU format, thesis-option eligibility, committee and iPOS, defense scheduling/format review deadlines; obtain chair approval. Mark institution-dependent completion unverified until confirmed.

## Completion standard
No scoring target, number of chapters, diagram, polished prose, passed software unit test or GitHub PR establishes thesis completion. The thesis passes only when requisite scientific and institutional gates are substantiated.
